original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Price one complete changed itinerary with both paid and productive histograms. Check #5693/#5698 for overlap and their exact hypotheses before another coframe search. Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Host frame 0 of the #7014 P104 factorisation as a product of root-line labels and charge every new monomial of that word, before touching the other twelve frames.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks whether a decoder or coframe change improves the full signed moment. Open PR #7014 asks a prior physical question: host one frame-indicator row as a legal label word and charge every new monomial before touching the other twelve. This package answers that first step for frame 0 only. It does not price a changed itinerary, so it cannot improve the signed moment.
bottleneck_link: A complete signed target bill needs the new charges of any legal producer that is added. This package records the 40 new monomials of one frame-indicator word and stops. Those charges are a prerequisite for pricing the thirteen rows together; they are not themselves a signed histogram or a supplier admission.
stop_rule: Stop after the length-4 word for frame 0, its 40 new monomials, and the statement that the other twelve frames are unexpanded. Do not convert the monomials into a selected-invoice histogram and do not claim a kappa change.
evidence: verify.py prints PASS_P104_ONE_FRAME_INDICATOR word=11,21,38,140 monomials=48 new=40. Evidence class: a written F2 factor restriction and a written reduction to (1+x0)(1+x1+x2+x4)(1+x5)(1+x6+x7), plus an exhaustive census of the 255 products of the only eight admissible letters. Not a heuristic. Not a selected-profile comparison. Selected kappa remains 781451/250000000.

open_questions.question: Which degree-at-least-2 monomials of frame 1 coincide with the 40 monomials charged for frame 0?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A shared monomial makes the joint bill of two rows smaller than the sum of the separate bills, which is the first interaction among the thirteen rows.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun the same census with frames[1] in place of frames[0] and intersect the two sets of degree-at-least-2 exponents.
open_questions.blocked_by: none in this alphabet; the other frame has not been expanded

open_questions.question: Can a sum of root-line letters host the frame-0 indicator with fewer than 40 new monomials in this chart?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 40-count is exact for products. A sum is a larger alphabet, so the product census is not a lower bound for it.
open_questions.first_step: Search linear combinations of the 120 letters, reduced in the simple-root chart, for a function that matches the indicator on all 120 lines and has fewer than 40 monomials of degree at least 2.
open_questions.blocked_by: the product census does not cover sums

open_questions.question: What is the selected #6030 invoice price of these 40 monomials, with no other rows attached?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Until each monomial is named as a paid primitive, the word cannot be compared with the selected profile and cannot change kappa.
open_questions.first_step: Match each of the 40 square-free monomials to a primitive the #6030 invoice already prices, or record that the match is undefined.
open_questions.blocked_by: this package does not identify those primitives
